City approves new transit plan

The city council voted on Tuesday to approve a transit plan that will add four new bus corridors and extend two existing rail lines over the next six years. The measure passed by a margin of seven to four after nearly five hours of public comment.

Supporters argued that the plan will cut average commute times for residents in the eastern districts, where bus service has lagged behind population growth for a decade. The new corridors are designed to connect neighbourhoods that currently require two transfers to reach the city centre.

Opponents raised concerns about the projected cost, which has risen by eighteen percent since the first draft was published last spring. They also questioned whether the construction schedule is realistic, given that the last rail extension finished two years behind plan and over budget.

Under the approved schedule, the first corridor opens in eighteen months, with the remaining three following at yearly intervals. The rail extensions are planned for the final two years of the programme, subject to a review of ridership data collected after the bus corridors begin service.

The mayor described the vote as the most significant investment in public transport in a generation. Officials said detailed design work will begin next month, and that public consultations on station locations will be held in each affected district before construction starts.
